articleTitle: STAR: A Mixed Analog Stochastic In-DRAM Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article addresses the optimization of data movement in accelerating machine learning workloads, one of the most critical issues of state-ofthe- art computing platforms. It presents a novel in-DRAM accelerator for convolutional neural networks using mixed analog-stochastic optimizations and shows significant energy-efficiency improvements. —Umit Ogras, University of Wisconsin, USA

articleTitle: Binary Forward-Only Algorithms
abstract: Today, the overwhelming majority of Internet of Things (IoT) and mobile edge devices have extreme resource limitations, e.g., in terms of computing, memory, and energy. As a result, training Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) using the complex Backpropagation (BP) algorithm on such edge devices presents a major challenge. Forward-only algorithms have emerged as more computation- and memory-efficient alternatives without the requirement for backward passes. In this paper, we investigate binarizing state-of-the-art forward-only algorithms, which are applied to the forward passes of PEPITA, FF, and CwComp. We evaluate these forward-only algorithms with binarization and demonstrate that weight-only binarization may be up to ~31× more efficient in terms of memory, with minor degradation in classification performance. Furthermore, we investigate and compare BP and forward-only algorithms in terms of binarization, finding that PEPITA and FF are more vulnerable to binary activations. The code is available at https://github.com/whubaichuan/BinaryFO.

articleTitle: Remote Power Side- Channel Attacks on FPGAs
abstract: Editor’s notes: Side-channel attacks, like those exploiting power and timing, are generally thought to require physical access to a system. This research challenges that idea by demonstrating how such attacks can be carried out on remote systems without physical access. It emphasizes the need to rethink how modern shared-FPGA systems are designed, prioritizing security as a core consideration. –Jeyavijayan Rajendran, Texas AM University, USA

articleTitle: Turbo-FHE: Accelerating Fully Homomorphic Encryption with FPGA and HBM Integration
abstract: The landscape of IT infrastructure shifted with the adoption of cloud computing, allowing organizations to use on-demand services, relieving them from owning IT infrastructure. However, this transformation comes with escalating concerns over privacy and security as the data processing is done on plaintext. If the cloud provider is malicious or vulnerable, the data of the users can be breached [1].

articleTitle: An Efficient Hardware Design for the VVC Prediction Refinement with Optical Flow
abstract: The Prediction Refinement with Optical Flow (PROF) is incorporated in the Affine Prediction of the Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard. While the Affine Prediction allows the representation of complex motions in the scene, the PROF enhances video encoding efficiency by generating a virtual rotation on each subblock of the current block. Due to the intensive computational processing, this work presents a dedicated hardware design for the PROF and its integration with the Affine Motion Estimation Reconstructor. The synthesis results show that the proposed PROF Core design can process 120 frames per second of 4K Ultra-High-Definition resolution videos while dissipating 2.2mW.

articleTitle: CAFEEN: A Cooperative Approach for Energy-Efficient NoCs With Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article proposes a reinforcement-learning-based methodology to improve energy-efficiency of Network-on-Chip-based systems. —Partha Pratim Pande, Washington State University, USA

articleTitle: Exploring Resilience of LPDRAM Against RowHammer
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article investigates, for the first time, how RowHammer attacks impact LPDRAM memories. The findings reveal that RowHammer causes bit flips at specific memory locations, which facilitates more predictable attacks.—Kanad Basu, University of Texas at Dallas, USA

articleTitle: Self-Sustainable Wearable and Internet of Things (IoT) Devices for Health Monitoring: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article discusses key challenges and opportunities to widespread adoption of wearable devices. It focuses on key challenges in the design and optimization, sensor data quality, energy sustainability, and privacy and security of wearable devices. For each challenge, the article reviews recent work and identifies future opportunities for research. —Ganapati Bhat, Washington State University, USA —Pietro Mercati, Intel Labs, USA

articleTitle: Understanding Error Propagation in Deep-Learning Neural Networks Accelerators and Applications
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are making their way into safety-critical systems, but they can be vulnerable to soft errors in hardware. Traditional duplication-based resilience methods are too expensive. This work studies how DNN inference’s deployment parameters impact error resilience via fault injection studies. Based on the error propagation analysis, it proposes new, efficient protection techniques specifically for DNN systems. This research laid the groundwork for further studies in DNN application resilience and safety.

articleTitle: ISCA: Intelligent Sense-Compute Adaptive Co-Optimization of Multimodal Machine Learning Kernels for Resilient mHealth Services on Wearables
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article proposes a sensing and computing adaptive optimization of multimodal machine learning kernels. The framework employs reinforcement learning to jointly determine sensing and compute configuration settings, which minimizes energy consumption while providing accuracy guarantees. The solution achieves up to 23% improvement in prediction accuracy compared to prior methods. —Ganapati Bhat, Washington State University, USA —Pietro Mercati, Intel Labs, USA

articleTitle: Still Making Noise: Improving Deep- Learning-Based Side- Channel Analysis
abstract: Editor’s notes: Side-channel attacks have been undermining cryptosystems for almost three decades. Advances in machine learning techniques have shown great promise in improving the performance and efficiency of side-channel attacks, even on systems with countermeasures. This article provides a systematic approach to applying ML techniques for side-channel attacks. —Jeyavijayan Rajendran, Texas A&M University, USA

articleTitle: Full Key Extraction of SNOW-V Using ML-Assisted Power SCA
abstract: Editor’s notes: Power side-channel analysis (SCA) attack represents a powerful means to leak secret key from a cryptographic hardware. This article demonstrates SCA-based complete secret key recovery for SNOW-V stream cipher, a communication standardization candidate for 5G network, and effectiveness of masking countermeasures. –Swarup Bhunia, University of Florida, USA

articleTitle: An EMG Denoising Method Based on Flexible Wearable Sensors
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article proposes an EMG denoising method that uses particle swarm optimization with wearable sensors. Compared to traditional denoising methods, the flexible electromyography sensor offers superior fit and wearability. The article verifies the proposed approach using self-acquired signals showing benefits over prior methods. —Ganapati Bhat, Washington State University, USA —Pietro Mercati, Intel Labs, USA

articleTitle: Reliability of Deep Neural Networks: Impact and Open Issues
abstract: Nowadays, Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are widely used in safety-critical fields such as automotive and healthcare, where their reliability is crucial due to their direct impact on human lives. Over the years, evaluating their resilience through software-level fault injection experiments has become a common research approach. The corruption of individual bits in the model’s parameters has been one of the most studied fault models in the last decade. This work introduces a methodology to evaluate the impact of permanent faults on DNN weights in image classification and object detection tasks, highlighting key ideas, main contributions, and the research’s impact over time.

articleTitle: A Coding Efficiency-Aware Hardware Design for VVC Affine Motion Estimation Reconstructor
abstract: One of the most important new tools of the Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard is the Affine Motion Estimation (AME). The AME contribution to the coding efficiency comes with a high computational cost, especially for real-time high-resolution video encoding, making dedicated hardware for battery-powered devices mandatory. Considering this scenario, this work presents a dedicated hardware design for the Affine Reconstructor of the VVC standard, focusing on high coding efficiency for real-time processing of UHD video. ASIC synthesis results show a circuit area of 179.9k Gates, with a power dissipation of 107.76 mW when targeting the processing of 4K UHD@60fps videos. The proposed design shows the lowest impact in BD-Rate (only 0.54%) in the current literature.

articleTitle: Background Receiver IQ Imbalance Correction for In-Field Testing
abstract: Editor’s notes: Direct-conversion receivers are used in integrated receivers and communication systems. This article proposes a methodology to measure IQ imbalance in direct-conversion receivers. —Partha Pratim Pande, Washington State University, USA

articleTitle: Compact and High-Performing Five-Stage Pipeline RISC-V Microprocessor Designed for IoT Applications
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article presents a compact and efficient five-stage pipeline RISC-V microprocessor by incorporating architectural optimization techniques for IoT applications. —Hiroki Matsutani, Keio University, Japan

articleTitle: CaSA: End-to-End Quantitative Security Analysis of Randomly Mapped Caches
abstract: Editor’s notes: Many security issues have recently been discovered in modern processors, leading experts to rethink their design. Since the cache-a critical part of modern processors-is often targeted by hackers to steal information, this research explores how well one popular defense, randomly mapped caches, works in protecting against such attacks. —Jeyavijayan Rajendran, Texas A&M University, USA

articleTitle: Toward Attention-based TinyML: A Heterogeneous Accelerated Architecture and Automated Deployment Flow
abstract: One of the challenges for Tiny Machine Learning (tinyML) is keeping up with the evolution of Machine Learning models from Convolutional Neural Networks to Transformers. We address this by leveraging a heterogeneous architectural template coupling RISC-V processors with hardwired accelerators supported by an automated deployment flow. We demonstrate Attention-based models in a tinyML power envelope with an octacore cluster coupled with an accelerator for quantized Attention. Our deployment flow enables end-to-end 8-bit Transformer inference, achieving leading-edge energy efficiency and throughput of 2960 GOp/J and 154GOp/s (0.65 V, 22nm FD-SOI technology).

articleTitle: Toward Standardized Vulnerability Assessment of Advanced Packaging Against Probing Attacks
abstract: The perpetual progression in semiconductor technology has led to the advent of heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced integrated circuit (IC) packaging techniques. These methods are pivotal for improving performance, reducing form factor, and enhancing the functionality of modern electronic devices. However, the complexity of these advanced packaging architectures inadvertently necessitates setting a new framework or standard for assessing vulnerabilities to hardware attacks, in particular probing attacks. This paper provides a nudge in the direction of developing a standardized quantitative method of assessing vulnerability of advanced multi-die packaging architectures to various probing modalities, such as nano-probing and electron beam (E-beam) probing techniques. These probing attacks present significant risks as they can be used to extract sensitive information or corrupt data communication channels, consequently compromising the confidentiality and integrity of systems where these devices are deployed. Through identification of potential vulnerable sites within package structure, proposal of vulnerability assessment criteria and vulnerability quantification metrics, and detailed empirical analysis of attack scenarios and case studies, this work serves as a pioneering effort towards elucidating the security threats that probing attacks introduce in these advanced packaging architectures. In addition, the paper presents a brief discussion on a range of potential countermeasures designed to mitigate the risks associated with probing attacks on advanced IC packaging.

articleTitle: Noise-Optimized Neuromorphic Spiking Radio in Context-Aware IoT
abstract: To bring Artificial Intelligence on the edge of Internet of Things sensing, this paper aims an RF neuromorphic spiking radio which is noise optimized to operate under stochastic resonance in weak inversion. The proposal is neuromorphic spiking radio using noise-optimized eNeurons. Results demonstrate a power consumption of 33 nW and an input power sensitivity of -31 dBm. Stochastic resonance favors a sensitivity enhancement of 9.5 dB, while energy efficiency is 33 pJ/bit and an area of 323 μm2. PVT analysis pointed out a reliable operation from 0 °C to 30 °C, achieving a fspike = 80 kHz (ie. 20 % degradation) and mismatch smaller than 10%.

articleTitle: Linear Algorithmic Checksums for Deep Neural Network Error Detection: Fundamentals & Recent Advancements
abstract: The widespread adoption of deep neural networks in safety-critical systems necessitates the examination of the safety issues raised by hardware errors. The consequent interest in fault tolerance methods that can deliver comprehensive coverage yet are sufficiently low-cost to meet the margin requirements of consumer deep learning applications can be satisfied through a rigorous exploration of the mathematical properties of the deep neural network computations. Concretely, this stringent set of requirements can be satisfied through a novel technique, Sanity-Check, that delivers error detection in fully-connected and convolutional layers through the use of linear algorithmic checksums. The interest in Sanity-Check was accentuated by its purely software-based implementation in a variety of off-the-shelf hardware platforms. Meanwhile, dedicated hardware extensions seamlessly integrate with modern deep learning accelerators and eliminate the performance overhead of the software-based implementation. The perfect critical error coverage of Sanity-Check offers a promising alternative for low-cost error detection in safety-critical deep neural network applications. The success of this approach in delivering frugal and highly comprehensive error detection has spurred a slew of subsequent research work, which we survey in this article.

articleTitle: Indirect Test Pattern Generation for Mixed-Signal Circuits Using Machine Learning
abstract: This work introduces a machine learning method for indirect test pattern generation in analog and mixed-signal circuits. The proposed method employs a low-cost test generation tool to simulate circuit specifications and parametric measures, incorporating variability via Monte Carlo simulation. Learning models are trained to relate low-cost DC node measurements to circuit specifications, enabling indirect testing. Validation on a 180 nm fully-differential integrated filter achieved R² scores of 0.76 for DC gain, 0.76 for cutoff frequency, and 0.98 for slew rate. A simulation fault injection campaign using a structural fault model (catastrophic and parametric faults) demonstrated 100% fault coverage with 19 measurements.

articleTitle: Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM): Requirements, Trends, and Opportunities
abstract: Editor’s notes: Silicon lifecycle management (SLM) is an integrated approach that encompasses the entire lifecycle of silicon-based hardware components, with a primary focus on integrated circuits and complex systems on chips. This article presents a thorough survey regarding various challenges associated with SLM. —Partha Pratim Pande, Washington State University

articleTitle: IC SEM Reverse Engineering Tutorial using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: In this tutorial, we will leverage artificial intelligence (AI) techniques to facilitate the reverse engineering of an integrated circuit based on scanning electron microspcopy, contributing to hardware assurance. This work encompasses various subjects, including image processing, computer vision, and machine learning, providing a comprehensive learning experience in these specialized domains. We encourage you to actively participate in this tutorial to execute your own project. The skills and knowledge acquired in this activity can bolster your resume, enhancing your prospects when seeking employment, pursuing further education, or advancing in your current professional role.

articleTitle: SuBhI: Securing Embedded System’s Runtime Integrity via Behavioural Information
abstract: Remote attestation (RA) is a vital security measure tailored for embedded devices.Numerous existing RA methods in the literature hinge on static analysis, validating binary integrity during loading but disregarding real-time integrity evaluation. This oversight might allow an attestation scheme to falsely succeed even with device compromise, thanks to runtime attacks like Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) and micro-architectural attacks. We have proposed a dual attestation scheme which ensures embedded device’s runtime integrity against control flow and micro-architectural attacks. A minor increase in executable size and less than 1 second increase in compilation time, the overhead is negligible for our proposal.

articleTitle: Adaptive Approximate Computing with CGRAgen
abstract: Modern Edge applications are diverse and compute-intensive but can often afford constrained computational inaccuracy. Commonly denoted approximate computing, this paper explores the integration of inexact arithmetic units into Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Array (CGRA) architectures with an associated, comprehensive framework for architecture modeling, hardware generation, and automated approximation, CGRAgen. A use case kernel from signal processing illustrates the functionality and potential of CGRAgen in design space explorations into CGRAs with integrated approximate computing techniques, highlighting the utility of making approximations reconfigurable.

articleTitle: GlucoseHD: Predicting Glucose Levels Using Hyperdimensional Computing
abstract: Editor’s notes: This article proposes an efficient algorithm to predict glucose levels using hyperdimensional computing. Highly accurate glucose level (GL) predictions are of critical importance for people affected by type 1 diabetes. To address this, the article proposes GlucoseHD, a hyperdimensional computing (HDC)-based approach for accurate GL predictions with limited computing and memory budgets. —Ganapati Bhat, Washington State University, USA Pietro Mercati, Intel Labs, USA

Recap of the 29th ACM/IEEE International Symposium on Low Power Electronics and Design (ISLPED’24)
abstract: The ACM/IEEE International Symposium on Low Power Electronics and Design (ISLPED) was brought back to the United States for the 2024 edition, after a successful 2023 edition in Vienna, Austria. The ISLPED’24 symposium was held on 5–7 August 2024, as an in-person event in the luxurious Hyatt Regency Newport Beach Hotel in the beautiful city of Newport Beach in Southern California. Two large conference rooms and several outdoor areas on the premises of the hotel were reserved for the symposium, providing ample space for presentations and networking among attendees.

Report on the 2024 Embedded Systems Week (ESWEEK)
abstract: Embedded Systems Week (ESWEEK) is the premier event covering all aspects of embedded systems and software. The event brings together three leading conferences (CASES, CODES+ISSS, and EMSOFT), one symposium, five hot-topic workshops, five special sessions, two panels, ten tutorials, seven education classes, two competitions with demos, one PhD forum, and a recruiting event. ESWEEK presents attendees with a wide range of choices unveiling state-of-the-art embedded systems design and hardware/software architectures. Besides, ESWEEK 2024 had a special panel to celebrate 20 years of ESWEEK.
